Article Title: 55 Indians still in Russian army: New Delhi presses Moscow at key meet, take action against agents
Article Text:
India continues efforts to secure the return of nationals serving in the Russian army (File photo)

NEW DELHI: Around 140 Indian nationals recruited into the Russian army have been discharged, while India is seeking information on the whereabouts of 55 others reportedly serving in the Russian armed forces, according to the details from India-Russia consultative committee meeting as cited by news agency ANI.New Delhi has engaged with Russian authorities for the early discharge of all such individuals."The government of India engaged with Russian authorities, including at the highest levels, for the early discharge of all such individuals. So far, around 140 Indian nationals have been discharged. Indian side is in touch with Russian authorities for the whereabouts of 55 Indian nationals who are reportedly in the Russian Army. Strong action being taken by the Indian law enforcement authorities against unscrupulous agents," the update from the meeting said.The latest figures are broadly in line with those shared by foreign secretary Vikram Misri last month. At the time, Misri said 139 of the 227 Indian nationals recruited into the Russian armed forces had been discharged, while 51 had died.Misri said the issue had been raised with Russia “at various levels on various occasions”.“At last count, we had information about 227 Indian nationals who had been recruited into the Russian army,” Misri had said. “Out of that, we have information that 139 of our nationals have been discharged from the army. And unfortunately, of course, we have information also about 51 people who have perished so far.”Misri had said India remained in constant discussions with Moscow to secure the early discharge and repatriation of those still serving.
Article Summary: New Delhi has engaged with Russian authorities for the early discharge of all such individuals. India is seeking information on the whereabouts of 55 others reportedly serving in the Russian armed forces. The latest figures are broadly in line with those shared by foreign secretary Vikram Misri last month.

Article Title: 'No evidence of fracture': Bengal govt to probe Mamata Banerjee's 2021 'injury'
Article Text:
Suvendu accuses Mamata of faking 2021 injury

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari on Saturday accused his predecessor Mamata Banerjee of faking her injury during the 2021 state assembly elections.Adhikari added that a fresh inquiry would be launched to probe Mamata Banerjee's “false claims” of injury. He claimed that there was no evidence of fracture or dislocation in the-then CM's medical report issued by treating hospital.“Mamata Banerjee faked her leg injury during campaigning in Nandigram in 2021. We have the medical report which stated that there was no evidence of fracture or dislocation. We will initiate an investigation into the matter,” PTI quoted Adhikari as saying at a press conference in Kolkata. He also displayed the TMC supremo’s medical report issued by the Bangur Institute of Neuroscience.“Her false allegation insulted the people of Nandigram. I will come out with more details after the MCC (model code of conduct) is lifted after October 9... Today, I am saying this in support of my claims made yesterday,” he added.His remarks came ahead of the Nandigram byelection scheduled for October 6. The counting of votes will be held on October 9.The Nandigram constituency was vacated by Adhikari after he defeated Mamata Banerjee in her Bhabanipore stronghold in the West Bengal assembly elections in April.He also won from Nandigram, his traditional seat, but chose to keep Bhabanipore.On March 10, 2021, Mamata Banerjee, the-then chief minister, sustained injuries to her left leg and waist while campaigning in the Reyapara area of Birulia in Nandigram.She initially alleged that a few unidentified people had deliberately pushed her against the door of her open car, causing it to slam into her left leg amid a heavy crowd.In a video message from the hospital, she said the “massive crowd” had pressed against her car while she was greeting supporters, causing her leg to be crushed and injured.The TMC supremo was diagnosed with severe bone and ligament injuries to her left ankle and foot, along with bruising and pain in her right shoulder, forearm, neck and waist. She was subsequently taken to Kolkata and admitted to the state-run SSKM Hospital.Mamata Banerjee was discharged two days later, on March 12, with her left foot in a cast. She subsequently resumed campaigning in a wheelchair.The TMC won 213 of the 294 seats in the 2021 assembly elections, while the BJP secured 77.However, the BJP won the 2026 assembly elections, securing 207 seats and forming its first government in West Bengal, while the TMC won 80 seats and was voted out of power after 15 years.
Article Summary: West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari accuses his predecessor Mamata Banerjee of faking her injury during the 2021 state assembly elections. He claimed that there was no evidence of fracture or dislocation in the-then CM's medical report issued by treating hospital.

Article Title: Jammu-Srinagar highway: 1 killed, 56 injured in twin accidents in J&K's Ramban
Article Text:
Passenger bus travelling from Srinagar to Jammu lost control. (Photo credit: X)

Tourist bus crashes into hillside

Rescue vehicle overturns

A tourist from West Bengal was killed and 56 people, including nine security personnel, were injured in two separate road accidents on the Jammu-Srinagar National Highway in J&K’s Ramban district on Saturday.The accidents occurred within half an hour and involved a passenger bus carrying tourists and a security vehicle that was on its way to assist in the rescue operation, PTI reported citing officials.The first accident took place around 8.50am near Maroog when a passenger bus travelling from Srinagar to Jammu lost control and collided with a hillside, officials saidThe bus, which had a West Bengal registration, was carrying tourists returning from a holiday in Kashmir. A woman passenger, identified as Jamuna from West Bengal, died in the accident, while 47 others were injured.Four of the injured: Suchitra, Lakshwanti, Kedar Patra and Fouji Ram, were referred to Government Medical College (GMC) Hospital in Jammu for treatment. The remaining injured passengers were stable and were expected to be discharged within a few hours, officials said.After receiving information about the bus accident, a Quick Reaction Team (QRT) of the Jammu and Kashmir Police and CRPF was rushed from the District Police Lines in Ramban to assist with the rescue operation.However, the security vehicle overturned near Kela Morh while travelling to the accident site, injuring six police personnel and three CRPF personnel, officials said. All nine injured security personnel were stable, they added.Jammu and Kashmir Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha expressed grief over the death and assured that the seriously injured would receive the best possible medical treatment."Deeply anguished by the tragic bus accident in Ramban, in which one person lost her life. Heartfelt condolences to the bereaved family. Spoke with DC (Deputy Commissioner) Ramban to ensure best possible treatment for the seriously injured shifted to GMC Jammu. Praying for their speedy recovery," Sinha said in a post on X.
Article Summary: A tourist from West Bengal was killed and 56 people, including nine security personnel, were injured in two separate road accidents on the Jammu-Srinagar National Highway. The accidents occurred within half an hour and involved a passenger bus carrying tourists and a security vehicle that was on its way to assist in the rescue operation.

Article Title: FSSAI steps up festive food crackdown as adulteration raids intensify
Article Text:
The regulator has specifically identified milk and milk products, sweets, snacks and savouries, edible oil, beverages and ghee for heightened scrutiny.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: With festive demand for sweets and milk products rising, food safety authorities have stepped up enforcement across the country, with thousands of kilograms of suspected adulterated food already seized or destroyed in Delhi-NCR. The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has now directed all states and Union territories to intensify inspections and sampling during Navratri and Diwali.In Delhi alone, food safety teams have destroyed more than 4,100 kg of suspected adulterated khoya and paneer during enforcement action last month, while samples of khoya, paneer, chhena and ghee are being collected from markets for testing.In neighbouring Mewat, officials have seized and destroyed more than 10,000 kg of adulterated paneer in last months, with around 50 raids conducted in areas identified as production hubs. Officials said the supply chain extends to Jaipur, Mathura, Gurugram, Faridabad and Delhi, raising concerns over the movement of adulterated paneer into the wider National Capital Region.Against this backdrop, FSSAI on September 29 directed food safety authorities across the country to step up surveillance and enforcement against adulterated, counterfeit and unsafe food products during the festive season.The regulator has specifically identified milk and milk products, sweets, snacks and savouries, edible oil, beverages and ghee for heightened scrutiny.States have been asked to conduct inspections and sampling at identified hotspots and sensitive locations. The directive also asks authorities to record inspection, sampling and outcome data on the Food Safety Compliance System (FoSCoS) and Food Safety Compliance through Regular Inspection and Sampling of Food (FoSCoRIS) on a real-time basis.The national directive also allows states to focus on products specific to local consumption patterns, including kuttu atta and singhada atta in northern and western regions.
Article Summary: With festive demand for sweets and milk products rising, food safety authorities have stepped up enforcement across the country. Thousands of kilograms of suspected adulterated food already seized or destroyed in Delhi-NCR. Food Safety and Standards Authority of India has directed all states and Union territories to intensify inspections and sampling during Navratri and Diwali.

Article Title: 'Could no longer defend the indefensible': Former AAP spokesperson Priyanka Kakkar joins Congress
Article Text:
Priyanka Kakkar joined the Congress. (IANS)

NEW DELHI: Former Aam Aadmi Party(AAP) spokesperson Priyanka Kakkar joined the Congress on Saturday, saying she could no longer defend the “indefensible”.Explaining her decision to leave AAP, Kakkar said, “There was a time when it was said that AAP would not take a bungalow or a car. But later, choppers started being used for private travel, and I could no longer defend the indefensible. ”“I drew a line when I saw that the Aam Aadmi Party, which at one point had attracted people with great substance and intelligence, was unable to retain them,” she added.She also questioned the appointment of people to senior positions in Punjab. “Who are the people being brought in now? New people who have not even worked at the booth level are being brought from Rajasthan and given senior positions in Punjab, along with bungalows and cars,” Kakkar said.“How long can I defend the indefensible?” she added.Kakkar also praised Congress leader Rahul Gandhi , calling him resilient and saying she had seen him and the party withstand attacks.“If there is one leader who is not afraid to promote his ideas, it is Rahul Gandhi. I observed that he is the only leader who has not shed tears for the cameras. He is the only leader today who has not done that. He is resilient. I have seen how he was humiliated and how an entire machinery was deployed to put him down.But Rahul Gandhi and the Congress remained resilient,” she said.“Their authenticity is their soul. I saw that there is a soul in this party as well, which I found missing in other parties. And I say this from lived experience,” she added.Kakkar also backed Rahul Gandhi's criticism of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over electoral-roll revision and his allegations concerning voters' rights.“I also saw how Rahul Gandhi has continuously launched a campaign against traitor Gyanesh Kumar. He has made everyone, including us, aware of this issue,” Kakkar said.“We have to make the public aware of how, according to him, our only voting right is being stolen by Gyanesh Kumar and put into PM Modi's account. This has to stop. Therefore, we must all come together now to support the Congress and support Rahul Gandhi in his authentic fight to keep the idea of India alive,” she added.Kakkar later called for opposition unity and urged people to join the Congress.“Now, we all have to come under one umbrella so that no votes are divided or scattered, because, as 'traitor' Gyanesh Kumar is already stealing votes and putting them into PM Modi's account. We must not give them any more opportunities. Everyone must come under one umbrella, under the Congress, to defeat PM Modi and his regressive politics,” she said.The Congress also said in a post on X that three prominent figures had joined the party, including, Priyanka Kakkar, former Uttar Pradesh MLA Shyam Sundar Sharma and journalist Rajat Rakesh Tandon.
Article Summary: Former Aam Aadmi Party spokesperson Priyanka Kakkar joined the Congress on Saturday. Kakkar said she could no longer defend the ‘indefensible’ Kakkar also praised Congress leader Rahul Gandhi calling him resilient and saying she had seen him and the party withstand attacks.

Article Title: Delhi Police registers 3 FIRs over protests demanding CEC Gyanesh Kumar's resignation
Article Text:
No individual or organisation has been named as an accused in the FIRs

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Delhi Police on Saturday registered three FIRs in connection with Friday’s protests by student organisations, political parties and civil society activists who attempted to gather at Jantar Mantar demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.Two FIRs were registered at Parliament Street police station and one at Connaught Place police station, a senior police officer said. The cases invoke Section 223 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), which deals with alleged disobedience of an order duly promulgated by a public servant.No individual or organisation has been named as an accused in the FIRs, the officer said. However, details of organisers and organisations that proposed or participated in the demonstrations have been included in the contents of the cases.The FIRs follow a day of protests across central Delhi, where thousands of opposition activists, students and youth organisation members attempted to march towards Jantar Mantar. Police detained around 1,000 protesters as they tried to cross barricades and reach the designated protest site.The demonstrations involved the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), All India Students' Association (AISA), Students' Federation of India (SFI), National Students' Union of India (NSUI), Indian Youth Congress (IYC) and other organisations.Protesters were demanding Kumar’s resignation over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and alleged mass deletion of voters.Police had repeatedly announced that gatherings were not permitted at Jantar Mantar. Protesters were stopped at several locations, including Firoz Shah Road and Ashoka Road, with some attempting to push past barricades. AISA president Neha Bora and several other activists were among those stopped.AAP leaders Saurabh Bharadwaj, Atishi and Sanjeev Jha were detained, while Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Singh was stopped while heading towards the protest. NSUI president Vinod Jakhar and activists from SFI and other student groups were also detained.Security was stepped up across central Delhi, with around 5,000 Delhi Police and paramilitary personnel deployed. Entry and exit gates at 12 metro stations were closed and internet services were suspended in parts of central Delhi amid the protests.
Article Summary: Delhi Police on Saturday registered three FIRs in connection with Friday’s protests by student organisations, political parties and civil society activists. Protesters were demanding resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Police detained around 1,000 protesters as they tried to cross barricades and reach the designated protest site.

Article Title: After Chandrayaan-3, ICMR asks scientists to attempt the ‘impossible’ in healthcare
Article Text:
Rs 8 crore on offer for health innovations that have never been tried anywhere in the world (Representativ e imaeg

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: After Chandrayaan-3 made India the first country to successfully land near the Moon’s south polar region, the government is now asking scientists to attempt something equally audacious in healthcare: develop something the world has never tried before.The Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) has launched its “First in the World Challenge”, inviting researchers to develop breakthrough vaccines, drugs, therapeutics, diagnostics and other health technologies that have never been thought of, tested or tried anywhere in the world.The initiative will offer up to Rs 8 crore for a single project, depending on how advanced the proposed innovation is. ICMR describes it as a high-risk, high-reward programme, acknowledging that some projects may fail but saying successful ones could bring about a major change in healthcare.The grants will be released in stages: up to Rs 1 crore for proof-of-concept, Rs 4 crore for prototypes and Rs 8 crore for final products or implementation models. Funding will be linked to deliverables, with ICMR reviewing each stage before approving the next.The opportunity is open beyond ICMR scientists. Researchers from government medical colleges, Institutes of National Importance, universities, recognised research laboratories and eligible NGOs can apply.Indian startups, micro, small and medium enterprises and industry are also eligible.The scheme targets genuinely new health technologies, not incremental improvements. ICMR will first check whether a proposal is truly “first in the world”, followed by assessment of its relevance and potential impact by a panel of experts, innovators, policymakers and scientists.The programme aims to take innovations from the lab to deployment, requiring researchers to detail regulatory, validation, commercialisation and technology-transfer plans, as well as demonstrate the technology’s clinical need, advantages over existing options and readiness for deployment.Applications will open on October 7 and close on November 30, with results due on December 31. Each proposal must include at least one co-principal investigator from the principal investigator’s institution. ICMR says the initiative is willing to back high-risk ideas with uncertain outcomes but potentially transformative gains, in pursuit of breakthroughs no one has achieved before.
Article Summary: The Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) has launched its ‘First in the World Challenge’ The initiative will offer up to Rs 8 crore for a single project, depending on how advanced the proposed innovation is. ICMR describes it as a high-risk, high-reward programme.

Article Title: Asian Games Medal Tally: India win 8 medals but remain outside top 10 as gold continues to elude
Article Text:

Shooting and kurash add to India's tally

NEW DELHI: India produced another strong medal haul at the Asian Games 2026 on Monday, winning eight medals across athletics, shooting and kurash. However, the impressive collection did not bring any change in the overall standings, with India remaining 12th as the country continued to wait for another gold medal.India added four silver and four bronze medals during the day but could not increase its gold tally. After Day 9, India stood at 45 medals — four gold, 20 silver and 21 bronze.'The eight-medal haul included silver medals for Yashvir Singh, Murali Sreeshankar, Gulveer Singh and Esha Singh, while Rohit Yadav, Parul Chaudhary, Vithya Ramraj and Pincky Balhara won bronze.India's strongest showing came in the men's javelin, where Yashvir and Rohit produced a double podium finish in the absence of defending champion Neeraj Chopra.Yashvir recorded a personal best of 85.72m for silver, while Rohit won bronze with 84.35m. Sri Lanka's Rumesh Pathirage claimed gold with 88.55m.Sreeshankar also won silver in the men's long jump with 8.07m despite an injury forcing him to abandon his final two attempts. China's Yuhao Shi took gold with 8.17m.Gulveer added his second silver of the Games with a personal best of 3:36.72 in the men's 1500m, having earlier finished runner-up in the 10,000m.Parul Chaudhary won bronze in the women's 5000m with 15:14.61, adding to the bronze she had claimed in the 3000m steeplechase.Vithya Ramraj also took bronze in the women's 400m hurdles with a personal best of 54.75 seconds.Esha Singh secured silver in the women's 25m pistol after finishing with 38 hits, the same score as China's Xiao Jiaruixuan, who won the gold after the shoot-off.Pincky Balhara added bronze in the women's -78kg kurash category, losing 0-5 to South Korea's Sumin Mo in the semifinals.Despite the eight medals, India's gold tally remained at four, a crucial factor in the standings as countries are ranked by gold medals first.China led with 132 golds, followed by Japan with 41, South Korea with 21 and Uzbekistan with 12. India remained 12th with 45 medals, highlighting how a large haul of silver and bronze medals has yet to translate into a significant rise in the standings.
Article Summary: India added four silver and four bronze medals during the day but could not increase its gold tally. After Day 9, India stood at 45 medals — four gold, 20 silver and 21 bronze. The eight-medal haul included silver medals for Yashvir Singh, Murali Sreeshankar, Gulveer Singh and Esha Singh.

Article Title: CJP protest: Scuffle breaks out near Shiv Sena Bhavan as supporters return from stir; watch
Article Text:
A scuffle erupted near Shiv Sena Bhavan in Dadar after a protest





MUMBAI: A scuffle broke out near Shiv Sena Bhavan in Dadar after supporters of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) returned from a protest at Shivaji Park.A video from the spot shows protesters arguing, with some allegedly hitting each other.The situation soon turned physical, prompting police to intervene and disperse those involved. Mumbai Police later said the situation was under control and peaceful.The incident followed a CJP protest at Shivaji Park over the party’s demands concerning Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar.Before the protest, a Dadar resident had opposed the demonstration. “They are doing it forcefully. This protest should not take place,” the resident said, adding that such demonstrations disturb peace in the area.The CJP has been demanding Kumar’s resignation and changes to the functioning and appointment process of the Election Commission. The Election Commission currently lists Gyanesh Kumar as the Chief Election Commissioner.Mumbai Police had earlier denied permission for the CJP to hold its October 2 protest at Shivaji Park. The party later announced a “Jail Bharo Andolan”.Meanwhile, a 75-year-old Thane resident died after suffering a heart attack while attending the CJP protest at Shivaji Park on Friday evening.The deceased was identified as Gopalakrishna Subbaiya Pillai, a resident of Dosti West County in Thane.Pillai arrived at Shivaji Park around 4.30pm to attend the protest. Around 5pm, he complained of chest pain. His friend and police personnel at the spot helped take him to Sushrusha Hospital in Shivaji Park.Police personnel tried to revive him with CPR before he was taken to the hospital, where he died while undergoing treatment. Police said doctors attributed his death to a heart attack.
Article Summary: A scuffle broke out near Shiv Sena Bhavan in Dadar after supporters of the Cockroach Janta Party returned from a protest at Shivaji Park. A video from the spot shows protesters arguing, with some allegedly hitting each other. The situation soon turned physical, prompting police to intervene and disperse those involved. Mumbai Police later said the situation was under control and peaceful.

Article Title: Flydubai attack: Co-pilot identified as Hamam Alhamami was barred from flying in Oman over 'extremist views'
Article Text:
As per reports, Alhamami had repeatedly expressed support for Palestinians and hostility towards Israel. His alleged views are being examined as part of a wider investigation into possible Islamic radicalisation and terrorist motives

Removed from Oman Air training role

Pro-Palestinian material found among belongings

Questions over clearance for Tel Aviv flight

Who is Hamam Alhamami?

What happened aboard flydubai flight

The Omani co-pilot accused of attacking Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar aboard a flydubai flight to Tel Aviv has been identified as Hamam Alhamami. He was barred from flying in Oman over concerns about his alleged extremist views.Al Arabiya English, citing sources, reported that he had spent much of his time outside Oman, particularly in Syria, where he was allegedly influenced by extremist ideas before travelling to the UAE.The revelations follow a CNN report that Alhamami had been removed from a training role at Oman Air, Oman's national carrier, last year. However, he was later given another role at the airline, the report said, citing a regional diplomatic source familiar with the matter.Further reports have raised questions about Alhamami's alleged ideological views. i24 News, citing an Emirati source, reported that leaflets and publications from “Free Palestine” groups, along with other pro-Palestinian material, were found among his belongings.According to the report, Alhamami had repeatedly expressed support for Palestinians and hostility towards Israel. The report said investigators were examining the material as part of a broader probe into his alleged Islamic radicalisation and possible terrorist motives.The reports have also raised questions about how Alhamami was cleared to serve on a Tel Aviv-bound flight despite being an Omani citizen. Oman does not recognise Israel and has no diplomatic relations with the country.An Israeli official told CNN that several agencies, including Shin Bet, Mossad, the military and the Transportation Ministry, were investigating how Alhamami came to be part of the flight crew.According to the report, Alhamami is an Omani citizen. He was born in the United Arab Emirates to an Omani father and Syrian mother and spent several years of his life in the UAE. The Jerusalem Post, citing sources close to the investigation, reported that he did not hold a second nationality.CNN reported that Alhamami had worked for flydubai for only eight months. He had previously worked for Royal Air Maroc, Morocco's national carrier.Alhamami was transferred from Saudi Arabia to the UAE after the aircraft made an emergency landing in Tabuk. He is facing a terrorism investigation in the UAE.The September 30 incident took place aboard a flydubai flight travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv. Alhamami allegedly attacked Captain Machchhar inside the cockpit in what is being investigated as a possible terror-driven attempt to bring down the aircraft.The confrontation triggered a steep descent, with the aircraft dropping approximately 16,000 feet within two minutes before a hijacking distress signal was transmitted.Despite suffering severe injuries, Captain Machchhar resisted the attack and managed to open the cockpit door. Flight crew members and passengers then entered the cockpit and restrained Alhamami, allowing the crew to regain control of the aircraft.Two non-duty aviators who were travelling aboard the flight also helped assume control of the aircraft. The plane subsequently made an emergency landing in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, with all 180 occupants disembarking safely.
Article Summary: Hamam Alhamami is the Omani co-pilot accused of attacking Captain Smit Machchhar aboard a flydubai flight to Tel Aviv. He was barred from flying in Oman over concerns about his alleged extremist views. Pro-Palestinian material was found among his belongings, according to reports.

Article Title: Of 97 left out in Goa, 88 are back, 3 others are Portuguese citizens: EC
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The office of the Goa chief electoral officer on Thursday said 88 of the 97 voters in the state whose names could not be included in the roll due to an alleged ECINet issue have been added back after their duly filled Form 6 was accepted. However, he also revealed that three of these 97 electors are Portuguese passport holders while six others were electors currently based outside India."In respect of voters who are currently residing outside India, officials are making efforts to establish and maintain contact with them for necessary action," the CEO said while sharing the status report on the 97 cases on X.Section 9 of the Constitution disallows dual citizenship. Goans born before 1961 in former Portuguese territories, as well as their kids and grandchildren, can apply for a Portuguese passport based on a citizen card issued by the Portuguese authorities after verifying their birth/descent documents. Portugal recognises dual citizenship; however, since dual citizenship is not allowed in India, anybody who acquires a foreign passport must surrender his Indian passport.As per Sec 9 of the Citizenship Act, 1955, a person's Indian citizenship automatically ceases upon acquiring foreign citizenship.Thus, three of the Portuguese passport holders in Goa may be classified as non-citizens, making them ineligible to be enrolled as Indian electors, said a source.Incidentally, Portuguese passport holders form 3% of the cohort of 97 electors for which the Goa CEO had repeatedly written to the EC after the ERO could not add them back via ERONet, leading the ECs to also raise questions on why access for such changes was 'centralised' and not available to the field officers. The issue was further amplified by the opposition parties after The Indian Express reported on the alleged internal notes of the election commissioners in this regard.EC sources on Thursday said the due diligence by the ERO the second time around may have served the purpose of SIR, as it is aimed at eliminating ineligible persons from the voters' list. Also, the fact that the issue was detected at the ERO level proves that the absolute right to add or delete a voter, based on verification, remains with the field officers, an EC officer told TOI.
Article Summary: 88 of the 97 voters in the state whose names could not be included in the roll due to an alleged ECINet issue have been added back after their duly filled Form 6 was accepted. NEW DELHI: The Delhi High Court has refused to grant bail to Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam in the UAPA case related to the 2020 Delhi riots.Senior Advocate Trideep Pais, appearing for Umar Khalid, submitted that there had been three “small changes in circumstances” since the earlier proceedings. He also referred the court to a Supreme Court judgment in support of his submissions.Pais pointed out that charges have not yet been framed in the case and, consequently, prosecution witnesses are yet to be examined. The court also noted that the charges were yet to be framed.Pais further submitted that a Special Leave Petition (SLP) is pending before the Supreme Court and that the trial court has indicated it would await the Supreme Court’s order. He then continued his submissions by referring to the Supreme Court judgment.Khalid and Imam had approached the Delhi High Court earlier this year after their bail applications were dismissed by the trial court for the third time on July 4. Imam was arrested in the case on August 25, 2020, while Khalid was arrested on September 13, 2020.The Delhi Police has opposed their bail pleas in the high court, asserting that the two were “masterminds” of the riots, PTI reported.The police argued that they could not seek bail on parity with other co-accused, stating that the Supreme Court had earlier categorised them as being part of the “command authority” and held that their “risk profiles” justified “continuing detention”.The police also argued that the present bail pleas were in the teeth of the Supreme Court’s January 5 order, which directed them to seek release only after the examination of protected witnesses was completed or after one year, whichever was earlier.On July 4, the trial court rejected Khalid’s bail application, saying it had “no option but to follow” the Supreme Court’s January 5 order and could therefore neither entertain the plea nor grant him relief.On September 2, 2025, a Delhi High Court division bench denied bail to Khalid and Imam. The Supreme Court upheld the verdict on January 5 but granted relief to co-accused Gulfisha Fatima, Meeran Haider, Shifa Ur Rehman, Mohammad Saleem Khan and Shadab Ahmad.A bench of Justice Aravind Kumar and Justice NV Anjaria had observed that there was a prima facie case against Khalid and Imam under the UAPA.On May 22, the Supreme Court granted six months’ interim bail to co-accused Abdul Khalid Saifi and Tasleem Ahmad, while referring to a larger bench the issue of prolonged incarceration of undertrials under the UAPA due to the stringent conditions for granting bail.
Article Summary: Delhi High Court refuses to grant bail to Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam in the UAPA case related to the 2020 Delhi riots. Delhi Police has opposed their bail pleas in the high court, asserting that the two were “masterminds” of the riots.

Article Title: Unsolicited advice to Supreme Court lands trial judge in trouble
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: It sounds inconceivable that a trial judge will advise the top court of the country on how to decide a case. But it happened recently, and the judge is now in trouble, with the Supreme Court seeking an explanation from him for advising it on when to grant bail.The case pertains to the bail petition of an accused from West Bengal who has been an undertrial prisoner for the last five years, and the apex court, while rejecting his plea, had asked the trial court to complete the proceedings within three months. The order, which was passed on May 11, directed the trial court to file a report after disposal of the case.As the trial court could not honour the SC order, the judge wrote to the apex court seeking more time to conclude the trial. But the judge, the additional district and sessions judge, 3rd court, North 24 Parganas at Barasat, also gave some unsolicited advice to the apex court on bail jurisprudence - when to grant bail and when not.After reading the letter, which was placed before a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran, the court expressed shock over its contents, which were uncalled for and directed its registry to ask the judge why he wrote what he wrote.The bench, however, did not reveal the exact wording of the letter but noted in its order that the judge conveyed words of advice."We are quite disturbed with the manner in which the trial judge has addressed a letter to this court requesting some more time. It is not for the presiding officer to convey words of advice as to when this court should grant bail and should not grant bail. The last two paragraphs of the letter are something which we have not appreciated. Registry to call for an appropriate explanation from the presiding officer at the earliest," SC said.The judge had written the letter dated Aug 11 addressed to the assistant registrar, Supreme Court, and prayed for some more time to complete the trial. Fixing the time for completion of the trial, SC in May had noted the case was proceeding at a snail's pace and asked that the trial be expedited as the accused had been languishing in jail for the last five years.Referring to a Calcutta HC order which had rejected the bail plea in March, saying all witnesses would be examined by the end of April, SC had said in its May order, "Although the HC was quite confident the remaining 12 witnesses would be examined by May 1, yet it seems not a single witness has been examined... We give one last chance to the state to proceed further with the recording of evidence of the remaining witnesses. We direct the trial court to see to it that the trial is completed within three months from today without fail."
Article Summary: The case pertains to the bail petition of an accused from West Bengal who has been an undertrial prisoner for the last five years. The apex court had asked the trial court to complete the proceedings within three months. The trial court could not honour the SC order, the judge wrote to the apex court seeking more time.

Article Title: Warring out, Pargat Singh in: Has Congress solved Punjab crisis or created more confusion?
Article Text:
Amrinder Raja Warring, Pargat SIngh

Warring is out, but not down

Amarinder Singh Raja Warring hints that Sachin Pilot may have played a role in his exit.

Amarinder Singh Raja Warring said he stepped down as Punjab Congress chief after reading the 'direction of the wind'

How the Channi-Warring tussle began

Warring out, but Channi not in

2022 rerun in Punjab

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The churn in Punjab Congress is now complete. Or is it?Amarinder Singh Raja Warring is out and Pargat Singh is the new Punjab Congress president. The change came hours after Warring resigned from the post, ending his more than four-year stint as state party chief. Warring met Rahul Gandhi on Friday and formally submitted his resignation. A day earlier, he had changed his X bio to “Former PPCC President”, signalling the leadership change."He (Rahul Gandhi) gave me a lot of love. He sought information about the current political situation in Punjab, on what is happening with the government and what we should be doing there," Warring said after his meeting.Hours later, the Congress announced the appointment of Pargat Singh as the new Punjab Congress president with immediate effect. The party also appreciated the contribution of outgoing president Warring.The change in Punjab Congress comes after months of infighting over who should lead the Congress into the 2027 assembly election. The crisis was triggered by Congress’s decision to retain Warring as state unit president in July, ignoring the claims of former chief minister Charanjit Singh Channi . So, Warring’s exit marks a victory for Channi and his supporters, but the entry of Pargat Singh means he does not gain from Warring's loss.Warring may be out of his post, but has dropped strong hints that his fight may be far from over. Hours after formally stepping down, Warring targeted his detractors, signalling he is not leaving the field yet. If Warring’s remarks against party incharge Sachin Pilot are an indication to go by, we could well see a reversal of roles in Punjab Congress infighting.In an interaction with news agency ANI, Warring said, “I feel that Sachin Pilot must have decided it was time to remove ‘Raja’ from the post.” Warring, though, added that he had “no concrete proof” of this.Warring added he had not spoken to Pilot about his exit, but had heard that the state Congress incharge may have recommended a change. “Perhaps the in-charge mentioned that Raja Warring would have to be replaced,” he said when asked about the reasons for his resignation.Taking digs at those responsible for his exit, Warring said nobody had formally asked him to resign. Instead, he had simply read the “direction of the wind”."Just like elder women who could tell by reading the direction of the wind whether it was going to rain... I observed the situation closely, and it never reached the point where someone had to ask me to resign," Warring told IANS.That, he said, was why he changed his X bio to “Former PPCC President” even before formally submitting his resignation to Rahul Gandhi.The timing and the turn of events are hard to miss. Nearly a month ago, Congress removed former Chhattisgarh chief minister Bhupesh Baghel as Punjab in-charge after the Channi faction openly rebelled against him. Baghel was accused of favouring Warring and was eventually replaced by Sachin Pilot.But now, Warring appears ready to open a front against Pilot and, of course, also Channi.That also raises questions about whether replacing Baghel with Pilot has actually helped Congress settle the Punjab crisis. Sugata Srinivasaraju, senior political analyst and author, believes that the leadership change appears to have created more confusion rather than resolving the crisis at hand."What is it that the Congress saw in Pilot that they did not see in Baghel? If you thought Baghel was part of the problem, now Pilot has also become part of the problem. He’s not part of the solution," he said.According to him, Congress may now have ended up with an even bigger problem. "All of them were against Warring. Now Warring goes out and Channi has not been catered to. So we don't know what's going to happen."Both Baghel and Warring are now out of their roles in Punjab Congress. For the Channi camp, it means one of their biggest demands has been met. But with Pargat Singh in the chair, will today's change end weeks of internal feud and bickering in Punjab Congress? Perhaps not.To understand why Warring’s exit and Pargat's entry may not be the end of the crisis, it helps to go back to where the tussle began.The crisis began on July 1, when the Congress leadership announced that Warring would continue as Punjab Congress president and Channi would head the campaign committee. Senior leaders Sukhjinder Singh Randhawa and Vijay Inder Singla were also given specific roles for the 2027 assembly election.On paper, it looked like an attempt to balance competing camps. In practice, it did the opposite.Channi’s supporters questioned why Warring was being retained as state chief and began pushing for a larger role for the former chief minister. What was meant to settle the leadership question instead reopened old faultlines within the party.Warring had been appointed Punjab Congress president after the party’s crushing defeat to AAP in the 2022 assembly election. Channi had been the party’s chief ministerial face in that campaign but lost both seats he contested.Warring was then brought in by the Congress high command (read Rahul Gandhi) to rebuild the organisation and prepare it for the next election. For nearly four years, however, the Congress did not clearly announce who would lead its 2027 campaign.When it finally tried to do that in July, the compromise pleased no one.Bhupesh Baghel, who was then Punjab in-charge, tried to defuse the tussle between the Channi and Warring camps but was also caught in the crossfire and forced out of the state.His replacement, Sachin Pilot, initially managed to bring the rival factions onto the same stage during the Congress protest over the Gulzar Singh suicide case. But that show of unity did not last long.What followed was another round of meetings, complaints and feedback to the high command and, eventually, Warring's exit and Pargat's entry.The Congress high command acted swiftly after Warring's exit and handed over the baton to Pargat Singh. The three-time Congress MLA from Jalandhar Cantt and former Indian hockey captain who has served as Punjab cabinet minister in Charanjit Singh Channi cabinet, has his task cut out.Pargat's name was doing the rounds along with other key contenders which included, former MLA Rana KP Singh, Raja Sansi MLA Sukhbinder Singh Sarkaria, former chief minister Charanjit Singh Channi and Gurdaspur MP Sukhjinder Singh Randhawa. But the frontrunner before today's appointment was former PWD minister and MP Vijay Inder Singla, who was appointed chairperson of the Congress Election Management and Coordination Committee in the July reshuffle."I am a loyal soldier of the party, and at all times, as a worker of the party, whatever responsibility I have been given, I have always fulfilled my duties. And in the coming times as well, we will work together with everyone in the same manner," Singla had said earlier reacting to speculations that he could replace Warring.However that did not happen.And this is where the leadership change in Punjab Congress becomes more interesting.The Channi camp had openly demanded that the former CM should lead the party into the next elections. In fact, their contention all along was that Warring should be replaced by Channi. But today's announcement would leave them disappointed much like the other contenders including Singla.With the Congress picking up Pargat Singh as the compromise candidate, it is a rerun of what happened in the run up to the 2022 elections.And that brings Punjab Congress back to a very familiar problem of bitter power tussle between state leaders. A problem that played a key role in the party’s defeat in 2022.Ahead of the 2022 assembly election, then chief minister Captain Amarinder Singh and Navjot Singh Sidhu were locked in a bitter leadership battle. Sidhu wanted a bigger role in leading the party into the election, while Amarinder resisted attempts to cut into his authority.The Congress leadership allowed the dispute to drag on until the crisis became impossible to contain. Eventually, Amarinder Singh was removed as chief minister. Charanjit Singh Channi emerged as the compromise candidate of Congress high command and was made the chief minister.But the compromise did not end the factional war. Congress went into the election divided and suffered a historic defeat, with AAP sweeping into power.Four years later, the names have changed, but the problem looks strikingly similar.Srinivasaraju sees a larger pattern in Punjab Congress's repeated leadership tussles."Punjab Congress has not been able to resolve it at all. They've had five long years after Amarinder Singh’s exit and they have still not got it right," he said.His argument is that every time Congress begins to see a chance of returning to power in Punjab, competing factions become more active and start weakening the organisation from within."We have seen that with Navjot Singh Sidhu and Amarinder Singh," he said, adding that similar mistakes "seem to be getting repeated".Once again, both the rival leaders - Channi and Warring - are out. But the battle for Channi is still half won. And with Warring all set for a rebel role, the road ahead for the former Punjab chief minister may not be easy.With Warring’s loss not translating into Channi's gain, it will be interesting to see if the Congress's compromise candidate ends this leadership fight once and for all without starting another power tussle?
Article Summary: Pargat Singh is the new Punjab Congress president. Amrinder Raja Warring resigned from the post, ending his more than four-year stint as state party chief. Warring may be out of his post, but has dropped strong hints that his fight may be far from over.

Article Title: India’s great hunt for oil: Inside the ₹84,000-crore Samudra Manthan mission
Article Text:
India is pushing for increased exploration of offshore oil and gas resources in various basins.

India's offshore oil hunt

From PM Modi's 2025 announcement to

Samudra Manthan

Where Rs 84,084 crore will go

Mahanadi is the immediate deepwater test

Mahanadi and Andaman in focus

Andaman is the frontier hunt

Krishna-Godavari is pushing deeper

Cauvery adds another deepwater target

The western offshore areas are also part of the plan

From geological potential to actual production

From discovery to production

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India is taking its search for oil and natural gas deeper into the sea.The focus is now spread across the Mahanadi basin off Odisha, the frontier waters of the Andaman-Nicobar region, and deeper sections of the Krishna-Godavari and Cauvery basins. The government's latest assessment puts the hydrocarbon potential of India's eastern and western offshore basins at more than 5,600 million metric tonnes of oil equivalent (MMTOE), with water depths extending to 3,000 metres.Recent discoveries in the Cauvery, Mahanadi and Andaman basins have strengthened the case for expanding offshore exploration.The push comes as India remains heavily dependent on imported energy. India is the world's third-largest consumer of crude oil and has an annual crude oil import bill of nearly $144 billion, or about ₹13 lakh crore, according to the government.There is another problem. Existing oil and gas fields naturally decline by around 6 to 7 percent each year. New discoveries are therefore essential to sustain domestic production.The current push is the latest stage of a decade-long effort to reshape India's upstream oil and gas sector.The government introduced the Hydrocarbon Exploration and Licensing Policy (HELP) in 2016 and launched the Open Acreage Licensing Programme (OALP). It also moved from Production Sharing Contracts to Revenue Sharing Contracts and expanded the National Data Repository.The government subsequently opened almost 99 percent of the offshore areas earlier classified as "No-Go" for exploration. This made more than one million square kilometres of India's Exclusive Economic Zone available for exploration.Prime Minister Narendra Modi gave the next phase a mission-mode identity in his Independence Day address on August 15, 2025.Calling the effort a modern-day "Samudra Manthan", PM Modi said India would work in mission mode to find oil and gas reserves beneath the sea. He also announced the National Deep Water Exploration Mission.On July 31, 2026, the Union Cabinet approved Samudra Manthan, the National Offshore Exploration Scheme. The central sector scheme, under the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, has an outlay of ₹84,084 crore through financial year 2030-31.The scheme allocates ₹28,534 crore for offshore seismic data acquisition, processing and interpretation, and ₹43,200 crore for 60 deepwater and ultra-deepwater exploration wells.The government will support up to 50 percent of eligible drilling costs, subject to a ceiling of ₹675 crore per well. The scheme also provides ₹10,000 crore for common offshore infrastructure, ₹2,000 crore for oil and gas manufacturing and services zones, and ₹350 crore for monitoring and support activities.But the real test of Samudra Manthan lies beneath the numbers.It is about where India is drilling, what it has already found, and whether those discoveries can eventually become producing fields.The Mahanadi Offshore Basin off Odisha is one of the most important tests of India's deepwater strategy.On July 25, Petroleum and Natural Gas Minister Hardeep Singh Puri marked the start of drilling of MN-DWN18-1-HD, the first appraisal well in the Mahanadi Offshore Basin.It is the first of four planned deepwater wells intended to systematically evaluate the basin, which the government considers one of India's most prospective offshore areas.An appraisal well is drilled to determine the quality and commercial potential of an existing hydrocarbon discovery. The four-well programme is therefore an important step beyond seismic interpretation. It is designed to establish how significant the basin's discoveries could actually be.Government records show that ONGC had already made two gas discoveries in the Mahanadi offshore area after the opening of the former No-Go zones. One of these was in a block where 94 percent of the area had earlier been classified as No-Go.But finding hydrocarbons is only the first step.The Mahanadi basin also highlights why Samudra Manthan includes a major infrastructure component. The government says several offshore discoveries remain undeveloped because production and evacuation costs are too high, particularly in the Mahanadi and Kutch basins.The scheme's ₹10,000 crore common infrastructure component is aimed at tackling that problem.Further east, the Andaman-Nicobar offshore basin represents a more frontier form of exploration.The government's 2017 Hydrocarbon Resource Assessment Study estimated hydrocarbon resources in the Andaman-Nicobar basin at 371 MMTOE. Following HELP, four blocks covering approximately 23,261 square kilometres were allocated for oil and gas exploration. Government data says exploration in those blocks generated 8,501 line kilometres of 2D seismic data, 3,270 square kilometres of 3D seismic data and three drilled wells.Another four blocks covering 47,058 square kilometres were subsequently offered in the Andaman basin under OALP-X.ONGC and Oil India have taken exploration into the ultra-deepwater region, with drilling operations targeting depths of up to 5,000 metres.One important well is ONGC's ANDW-7 in the East Andaman Back Arc region. The well encountered traces of light crude and condensate in cutting samples, C-5 neo-pentane in trip gases and reservoir-quality facies. The government said the findings provided evidence of an active thermogenic petroleum system in the region, comparable with petroleum systems in Myanmar and North Sumatra.The findings do not establish a commercially producing field. The government has said commercial reserves in the Andaman campaign remain to be established. Their significance lies in providing evidence of a working petroleum system that can guide further exploration.The Krishna-Godavari basin off India's eastern coast is a more established offshore hydrocarbon province but remains central to the country's deepwater strategy.In OALP Round VIII, the 2022 KG-UDWHP-2022/1 ultra-deepwater block in the Krishna-Godavari basin covered 1,199.64 square kilometres. This was the size of that particular block, not the total current exploration acreage of the basin.The Krishna-Godavari basin has also attracted international technical collaboration. In 2022, ONGC signed a Heads of Agreement with ExxonMobil for deepwater exploration covering the Krishna-Godavari and Cauvery basins on the eastern coast and the Kutch-Mumbai region on the western coast.The Cauvery Offshore Basin is another important part of India's eastern offshore exploration map.The government's 2026 Samudra Manthan backgrounder cites recent finds in the Cauvery, Mahanadi and Andaman basins as evidence supporting the broader offshore opportunity.The basin is part of India's wider effort to identify additional offshore resources through deeper and more technically demanding exploration.Samudra Manthan is not confined to India's eastern coast. The western offshore belt, including Kutch and Mumbai Offshore, is also part of the country's wider exploration strategy.The government has identified Mahanadi and Kutch as areas where common offshore infrastructure is particularly important because high production and evacuation costs can prevent discoveries from moving into production.OALP Round VIII in 2022 included blocks in Mumbai Offshore, Kutch, Saurashtra and Kerala-Konkan. ONGC's collaboration with ExxonMobil also covered the Kutch-Mumbai region, keeping the western offshore belt within India's broader deepwater exploration push.The numbers attached to Samudra Manthan describe a large opportunity, but they do not mean India already has 5,600 MMTOE of proven offshore reserves waiting to be produced.The government estimates more than 5,600 MMTOE of hydrocarbon potential across India's eastern and western offshore basins. Separately, subject to exploration success, Samudra Manthan aims to add more than 600 MMTOE of hydrocarbon reserves, expand the country's hydrocarbon resource base from 1.6 billion tonnes of oil equivalent to 2.2 billion tonnes of oil equivalent, and increase annual domestic oil and gas production from around 62 MMTOE to 80 MMTOE.The government says the additional production could eventually reduce crude oil imports by nearly ₹1 lakh crore a year.The distinction between potential, reserves and production is critical. Seismic surveys identify promising geological structures, but drilling is required to establish whether hydrocarbons are actually present. A discovery then needs appraisal, reserve estimation and commercial assessment before it can move into development and production.Samudra Manthan therefore goes beyond drilling. Its ₹84,084 crore framework combines geological data acquisition, deepwater drilling support, common infrastructure, and domestic manufacturing and services capacity.The immediate picture is spread across different stages. Mahanadi is in an appraisal campaign designed to evaluate hydrocarbon discoveries. Andaman remains a frontier basin where geological evidence points to an active petroleum system, but commercial reserves have yet to be established. Krishna-Godavari and Cauvery remain important eastern offshore targets for deeper exploration, while Kutch and other western offshore areas form part of the wider exploration and infrastructure strategy.Samudra Manthan is therefore not simply India's ₹84,084 crore plan to drill more wells. It is the latest stage of a decade-long effort to open offshore acreage, improve geological data, encourage exploration and build the infrastructure needed to bring commercially viable discoveries into production.The decisive test will be whether prospects beneath the Mahanadi, Andaman, Krishna-Godavari, Cauvery and other offshore areas can make the journey from geological potential to commercially recoverable reserves and, finally, to actual oil and gas production in India.
Article Summary: India is taking its search for oil and natural gas deeper into the sea. The focus is now spread across the Mahanadi basin off Odisha, the frontier waters of the Andaman-Nicobar region, and deeper sections of the Krishna-Godavari and Cauvery basins. Prime Minister Narendra Modi gave the next phase a mission-mode identity in his Independence Day address on August 15, 2025.

Article Title: Punjab CM Mann says Rs 1,262 crore Satkar Rashi released to 36.87 lakh women

Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Singh Mann on Thursday said Rs 1,262.54 crore was being transferred directly into the bank accounts of 36.87 lakh women under the state government’s Mawan Dheeyan Satkar Yojna.The amount constitutes the second instalment under the scheme and covers October, November and December, Mann said while addressing a function at Khandoor Sahib. Each beneficiary would receive the three-month instalment together, he said.According to Mann, Rs 2,562.33 crore had previously been distributed among 73.99 lakh women. With the latest disbursement, the total amount transferred under the scheme has reached Rs 3,824.87 crore, he said.Mann said around 97% of women in Punjab would be eligible for the scheme and that the government had set a target of extending its benefits to one crore women. He also said there were no conditions limiting the number of eligible women in a household, meaning that if three women in a family qualified, all three could receive the assistance.The chief minister said 1.37 lakh Satkar Sakhis had helped register women under the scheme and had received more than Rs 51 crore in incentives.Anganwadi workers involved in facilitating registrations would also receive incentives totalling Rs 25 crore, he said.At the event, Mann also criticised opposition parties and said that if the Congress, BJP or Akali Dal came to power, schemes including the Satkar Yojna, free bus travel for women and free electricity would be discontinued. These were political claims made by the chief minister.Mann also targeted the Congress and Shiromani Akali Dal, commenting on their internal political situation. He said the Congress had fewer workers but more leaders aspiring to become chief minister and alleged that the Akali Dal had misused religion.Referring to the state government's performance since 2022, Mann claimed that Punjab had moved from 27th to first position in school education according to the Centre's assessment. He said the government had established smart classrooms, trained teachers and recruited non-teaching staff.On medical education, Mann said around 30 lakh students appear for NEET every year and claimed that the number of students from Punjab's government schools clearing the examination had risen from 80 when he took office to 882 this year. He said the state had introduced free coaching for government-school students.Mann also said the government would open new centres for UPSC preparation to help students from Punjab prepare for the civil services.On power supply, the chief minister said eligible households were receiving 300 units of free electricity each month. He also said the state government had purchased the Goindwal Sahib Thermal Power Plant for Rs 1,080 crore.Mann said farmers were receiving daytime electricity for agricultural use and claimed that 14,000 kilometres of pipelines had been laid to take canal water to fields.He also said the pace of development in Punjab would increase between 2027 and 2032 as projects undertaken during the current government's tenure begin to show results.Cabinet minister Harbhajan Singh ETO and others were present at the event.
Article Summary: Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Singh Mann said Rs 1,262.54 crore was being transferred directly into the bank accounts of 36.87 lakh women. The amount constitutes the second instalment under the scheme and covers October, November and December. Mann said around 97% of women in Punjab would be eligible.

Article Title: Pacific to pacify ties? Washington sends US admiral to India as relations face strain
Article Text:
Samuel Paparo's visit comes after a run of statements in Washington.

Press release by the US Embassy in India.

What Washington has put on record

The China question in the background

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: American admiral Samuel J. Paparo, who leads US Indo-Pacific Command, is in India from 3 to 8 October. It is his second visit this year.The US Embassy said the trip is meant to push forward the "major defense partnership" and deepen cooperation between the two militaries.Its list of topics includes digital transformation, emerging technologies and regional strategic stability. It also names "defense energy resilience" and an "increasingly competitive technology landscape", though it does not spell out what either would involve.On his earlier trip, Paparo visited Delhi, Chandimandir and Bengaluru. He met the Chief of Defence Staff and the Navy chief, and discussed security along India's western and northern borders.Last month, Paparo conducted a series of key bilateral and multilateral meetings on the sidelines of the 28th Indo-Pacific Chiefs of defence conference in Victoria, Canada, held from August 31 to September 2.According to the US Pacific Command (US PACOM), Paparo highlighted "the importance of strong bilateral and multilateral relationships in advancing regional security and deterrence".Throughout the conference, the US commander engaged in discussions with the Defence Cooperation Council and the Quadrilateral Security Dialogue (Quad), and joined military leadership from Asean nations.Paparo also connected with defence counterparts from Australia and the United Kingdom for an Aukus dialogue, and conferred with Adm. Giuseppe Cavo Dragone, chair of the Nato Military Committee.US Pacific Command noted that Paparo carried out bilateral discussions focused on "strengthening operational cooperation, information-sharing, maritime security and readiness across the Indo-Pacific" with senior representatives from numerous partner nations.The participating countries included Bangladesh, Brunei, Cambodia, Canada, France, India, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, Mexico, Mongolia, New Zealand, the Republic of Korea, Singapore, Thailand, and Vietnam.Paparo's visit comes after a run of statements in Washington. An update on how the 2026 National Defense Strategy is being carried out, sent to the Senate Armed Services Committee, places India under the heading of burden-sharing, the idea that allies and partners should take on more of the load."Finally, and crucially given its regional standing and power, we are also building on our strong defence relationship with India, with the recent signature of a 10-year bilateral defence framework and a separate framework to strengthen undersea cooperation," the update said.Testifying before lawmakers in April, Paparo said the relationship with India had seen "transformative growth through increasingly complex military exercises, defence sales, and strategic dialogue".However, the recent Trump tariffs and the punitive measures against India for buying Russian oil, and a stuck trade deal has undoubetly strained the ties between both nations.Paparo had also pointed to cooperation on maritime security and underwater awareness, including India's planned purchase of MQ-9B drones through US foreign military sales. He also described India as one of the partners he visits and coordinates with most often.He said India "continues to be a source of stability within South Asia", and cited its investments in Sri Lanka and its agreements with Mauritius, which he said help keep strategic infrastructure "free of adversarial influences". On Pakistan, he noted that recent military exchanges had extended beyond traditionally disputed areas, but said India's main focus remained "maintaining deterrence and credible warfighting capability within the region writ large. "None of this is discussed in isolation from China as Paparo himself has said Beijing's actions, along with its deepening ties to Russia and North Korea, make for a complex challenge to regional stability. He calls alliances and partnerships Washington's "greatest asymmetric advantage", and the Quad, which brings together the US, India, Japan and Australia, is part of that picture. Though Quad his been pushed to a back burner under the Tump 2.0.At a regional security conference in Malaysia, Paparo said some actors were using "false claims of legitimacy" to justify coercion. "That's not the rule of law. That's the rule by law. That distinction between law as a tool of order versus law as a weapon of raw power, is the defining fault line of our time," he said. He added that the US was deterring China "through strength, not through confrontation".In the South China Sea, Manila has accused Beijing of dangerous manoeuvres, water cannon attacks and attempts to block resupply missions around a disputed shoal. China denies this. Philippine defence secretary Gilberto Teodoro said, "China is everywhere … this is a matter of concern," and pointed to a recent Chinese ballistic missile launch into the Pacific.At the congressional hearing, Representative Adam Smith said partners needed reassurance. "We need to maintain those relationships. We need to let those folks know that we are there and they can depend on us," he said.
Article Summary: American admiral Samuel J. Paparo, who leads US Indo-Pacific Command, is in India from 3 to 8 October. It is his second visit this year. US Embassy said the trip is meant to push forward the "major defense partnership" and deepen cooperation.

Article Title: Nearly half of India’s medical colleges fail to comply with NMC disability-unit directive
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Nearly half of India’s medical colleges (44.5%) have failed to set up Enabling Units mandated by the National Medical Commission for students with benchmark disabilities. Of 798 colleges, 355 remain non-compliant, with several naming sanitation inspectors, residents, tutors and head clerks as single points of contact, according to an affidavit filed by the Commission in the Supreme Court on Tuesday.At Maharashtra Government Medical College, Nandurbar, a sanitation inspector, has been designated as the coordinator of the Enabling Unit. Other colleges have named residents, tutors and head clerks as points of contact.Dr Satendra Singh, disability-rights activist and doctor associated with Doctors with Disabilities: Agents of Change, questioned the choice of personnel for the role. “It’s unheard of for a sanitation inspector or head clerk to be made in-charge of such a committee in a medical college. They have neither the designated administrative or academic responsibility for undergraduate or postgraduate training nor the training or authority to deal with disability accommodation, clinical training, patient safety or assessment.He added, “They cannot take or escalate decisions on postings, duty hours, assistive devices, accessible infrastructure, examination accommodations or clinical-rotation modifications. Tutors and residents are also a floating population, often at an institution for only a limited period. How would a postgraduate student in pharmacology, who may not even be an alumnus of that institution, know what assistance a wheelchair-using medical student needs in an operation theatre or have the authority to direct the theatre staff?”The NMC circular does not prescribe a doctor or clinical faculty member as the single point of contact. It does, however, assign the Enabling Unit responsibility for reasonable accommodation, academic and clinical support, barrier-free access, coordination, record-keeping and information dissemination.The compliance exercise was undertaken following the Supreme Court’s August 4, 2026 order in Anmol vs Union of India, which directed the NMC to seek college-wise compliance with its July 27 circular through Deans and Principals.The court warned that if colleges failed to respond or follow the directions, “a serious view will be taken against the individual colleges.”The NMC’s affidavit said 515 of 798 colleges had responded by September 28: 443 reported full compliance, 26 partial or ongoing compliance, and 46 submitted only the committee-constitution order. As many as 283 colleges did not respond. Majority of NMC-designated medical assessment boards and appellate boards themselves fail to comply, despite NMC warning that “serious view” would be takenThe commission had set September 10 as the deadline and issued reminders on September 23 and 24, the latter warning that late submissions would not be accepted and show-cause notices would follow. Article Title: The average will never applaud the exceptional
Article Text:
The Final Problem’

“Venmai Enappaduvadhu Yaadhenin, Onmai

Udayam Yaam Ennum Serukku.”

“What is mediocrity? It is the vanity that declares, ‘I am wise.’”

A doctor by profession, Arthur Conan Doyle travelled to the Arctic, supported the early use of vaccines when they were still viewed with apprehension, and wrote poetry, drama, history and fiction. He was also an enthusiastic sportsman and introduced skiing in Switzerland’s Alps mountains.But none of these achievements would define his place in popular imagination as the creation of one character: Sherlock Holmes.Holmes became legendary because he was more than a detective. He observed what others overlooked, questioned what others accepted and followed reason where intuition might have led people astray. Doyle gave him a mind of extraordinary precision.There were interesting contradictions between the author and the character he created. Holmes does not believe in ghosts, but Doyle deeply believed in conversations with spirits!Some of the quotations by Holmes are intense and sets you to think. “There is nothing more deceptive than an obvious fact.” “When you have eliminated the impossible, whatever remains, however improbable, must be the truth.” And, with characteristic arrogance, he declares, “I am my brain, the rest of me is merely an appendix.”Doyle eventually grew frustrated that Holmes had overshadowed everything else he had written. So, in ‘, published in 1893, he killed Holmes, sending him and his arch-rival Professor Moriarty plunging to their deaths at the Reichenbach Falls.The readers could not accept this.There was outrage and thousands of cancellations of magazine subscriptions. Doyle had underestimated the bond between Holmes and his readers. Eventually he resurrected him in another story.Among Holmes’s many quotations, one particularly catches my attention:“Mediocrity knows nothing higher than itself. But talent instantly recognises genius.”There is something profound in both halves of that sentence.Mediocrity is not necessarily a lack of talent, nor is something to be looked down upon. The danger lies elsewhere: when comfort becomes a reason not to acknowledge efforts of others. The word mediocrity has a Latin root that means – ‘halfway up the mountain’.Perhaps that is why the mediocre mind often struggles to acknowledge greatness. When someone spends years pursuing a mission; a writer writing, an artist creating, an entrepreneur building, a reformer changing, there may be someone who asks, “But he did not make any money” or “She did not take care of her family”. Lest they understand that the pursuit for greatness is fulfilling in itself.And that is where the second half of Holmes’s observation becomes even more powerful.‘Talent recognises genius’.Helen Keller, deaf and blind, met M S Subbulakshmi when she visited India in 1955. When MS began to sing, Keller gently placed her fingers on the singer’s throat, sensing the vibrations of the music. Deeply moved, she is remembered for telling MS, “You sing like an angel.”How beautifully one extraordinary person spotted another.Long before Holmes, Thiruvalluvar had captured the human weakness of mediocrity with astonishing precision. In Kural 844, he says:The mountain does not become smaller because someone has stopped climbing.And greatness may simply be the courage to keep looking upward.
Article Summary: Holmes became legendary because he was more than a detective. He observed what others overlooked, questioned what others accepted and followed reason where intuition might have led people astray. The word mediocrity has a Latin root that means – ‘halfway up the mountain’

Article Title: 5 Indian seafarers safely rescued after Kuwait-flagged tanker struck by projectile in Strait of Hormuz

(Representative image): The Indian nationals were aboard MT Kazimah III, which was hit while sailing through the strategic waterway. The embassy coordinated their rescue and said all five had been safely shifted ashore.
