Five Indian nationals aboard a Kuwait-flagged crude oil tanker were safely rescued after the vessel was struck by a projectile in the Strait of Hormuz, the Indian embassy in Oman said on Friday.The Indian nationals were aboard MT Kazimah III, which was hit while sailing through the strategic waterway. The embassy coordinated their rescue and said all five had been safely shifted ashore.“Earlier today, the Mission coordinated rescue of five Indian nationals on board the Kuwait-flagged tanker MT Kazimah III, struck by a projectile in the Strait of Hormuz. All 5 Indian nationals have been shifted ashore safely. We thank the Omani authorities for their continued support and assistance,” the embassy said in a post on X.The embassy thanked Omani authorities for their support during the rescue operation.MT Kazimah III is a crude oil tanker sailing under the Kuwaiti flag and was en route to the port of Lomé in Togo when it was struck.The incident comes as India steps up efforts to monitor the safety of its seafarers amid heightened security risks in the Persian Gulf and other major shipping routes.Earlier on Tuesday, external affairs ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said that more than 4,500 Indian seafarers were aboard commercial vessels operating in the region. Of these, 163 were on 12 active cargo ships, including six India-flagged vessels and six foreign-flagged vessels carrying cargo to India.“At this point, we have six India-flagged commercial vessels in the Persian Gulf. We also have six foreign-flagged vessels which are carrying cargo to India. So 12 ships are there. On these ships, we have around 163 Indian seafarers who are on board,” Jaiswal said during a media briefing.“Apart from this, we also have over 4,500 Indian seafarers who are on board various commercial vessels which are operating in the area,” he added.Jaiswal said the ministry of shipping was coordinating with Indian diplomatic missions and local stakeholders to track vessel movements and monitor the welfare of Indian seafarers.“Our ministry of shipping continues to monitor the movement of these ships and is looking at the well-being of all these seafarers, and as and when required, through our embassies and other stakeholders, they do the needful for their well-being and welfare,” he stated.“On our side, we remain committed to the safety and well-being of our seafaring community abroad,” Jaiswal said.The incident comes amid growing risks to commercial shipping across the Persian Gulf, Red Sea and Black Sea, where vessels have faced repeated attacks.External affairs minister S Jaishankar had raised concerns over attacks on commercial vessels and seafarers during his address to the 81st United Nations general assembly last week.“New challenges in the maritime domain have added to longstanding ones on land. There have been attacks on commercial shipping and seafarers in the Gulf and from the Red Sea to the Black Sea. Indian seafarers have lost their lives, as have others from other nations.This is completely unacceptable,” Jaishankar told the UN assembly.Jaishankar said India had joined Liberia and 23 partner nations in an international coalition aimed at mobilising global public opinion and defending commercial shipping routes.“We must ensure that the safety and security of shipping and seafarers is never compromised. Scrupulously observing international law is an integral element of that endeavour,” Jaishankar urged.He also called for immediate restraint and de-escalation in the Gulf to protect civilian crews and ensure the uninterrupted movement of energy supplies and global trade.
Article Summary: The Indian nationals were aboard MT Kazimah III, which was hit while sailing through the strategic waterway. The embassy coordinated their rescue and said all five had been safely shifted ashore. The incident comes amid growing risks to commercial shipping across the Persian Gulf, Red Sea and Black Sea.

Article Title: Can't invoke anti-slaughter law in case of mere illegal cattle transportation: SC
Article Text:
Acquitting a person convicted by a trial court and Chhattisgarh HC for illegally transporting 32 bulls under Chhattisgarh Agricultural Cattle Preservation Act, 2004, a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said police have failed to establish the intention of the accused.

NEW DELHI: At a time when vigilante groups are active in stopping cattle smuggling purportedly to prevent slaughter, the Supreme Court has ruled that the police cannot presumptively invoke stringent provisions of anti-cattle slaughter laws against people for mere illegal transportation of bovine animals.Acquitting a person convicted by a trial court and Chhattisgarh HC for illegally transporting 32 bulls under Chhattisgarh Agricultural Cattle Preservation Act, 2004, a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said police have failed to establish the intention of the accused that cattle were being transported for slaughter. The prosecution said the intercepted truck did not have any document that authorised the driver and cleaner to transport cattle from Chhattisgarh to Odisha."The mere fact that the transport was not accompanied by any documents cannot lead to a presumption that it was for slaughter," SC said. "We find no reason to uphold the conviction, especially when a veterinary doctor and the 'Gaushala Committee' chief said before the court that the seized cattle were fit for use in agriculture."
Article Summary: Supreme Court rules that police cannot invoke stringent provisions of anti- cattle slaughter laws against people for mere illegal transportation of bovine animals. Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said police have failed to establish the intention of the accused.

Article Title: Cases clubbed only after CJI spoke to presiding judges
Article Text:
The contempt petition was initiated for the alleged violation of the SC's May 23, 2025, judgement directing the gradual reduction and eventual phasing out of IPS officers' deputation to CAPFs and is pending before a bench headed by Justice Ujjal Bhuyan.

NEW DELHI: The sound and fury in the Supreme Court Wednesday over the clubbing of two petitions - one seeking the initiation of contempt proceedings for the violation of an earlier SC judgement and the other challenging the validity of a new law - both on the deputation of IPS officers in the central armed police forces (CAPFs), has turned out to be much ado about nothing.The contempt petition was initiated for the alleged violation of the SC's May 23, 2025, judgement directing the gradual reduction and eventual phasing out of IPS officers' deputation to CAPFs and is pending before a bench headed by Justice Ujjal Bhuyan.Another petition, which challenged the validity of the new CAPF Act, which was enacted subsequent to the SC judgement and permitted the deputation of IPS officers to CAPFs, is before another bench headed by Justice Manoj Misra.On September 30, the contempt petition listed before Justice Bhuyan was abruptly dropped from the notified list of cases, and, subsequently, both the contempt petition and the writ petition were listed before a special bench of Justices Misra and Bhuyan. This led to an uproar before the special bench. Senior advocate Shyam Divan said, "You cannot have a listed matter plucked off the board. This is an all-India court.People make travel arrangements and come here from all over the country. Why should a matter which is listed be removed during the course of the day? Once the cause list is mentioned and notified in the Supreme Court of India, no one can fiddle with it." Senior advocate Guru Krishna Kumar echoed Divan's grievance.However, it transpired that additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati had requested that the two petitions be clubbed and be placed for hearing before any one of the two benches on the ground that the new law was the defence of the Union govt in contempt and suggested that it would be better if the two cases were heard together.SC registry sources said following this, the CJI consulted the presiding judges - Justices Misra and Bhuyan - before constituting the special bench and placing both the matters before it.However, Justice Misra faulted the ASG for not informing the opposite side prior to making the request to the CJI, which led to such a situation. The CJI could not be contacted, as he is abroad.The SC registry, from which an explanation was sought, filed a report on clubbing of the two cases. The bench of Justices Misra and Bhuyan said in its order, "The explanation tendered by the registry is accepted and taken on record. The same shall be kept in a sealed cover by the concerned section." It posted both the contempt petition and the writ petition for hearing together on Oct 15.
Article Summary: The contempt petition was initiated for the alleged violation of the SC's May 23, 2025, judgement directing the gradual reduction and eventual phasing out of IPS officers' deputation to CAPFs. Another petition, which challenged the validity of the new CAPF Act, which was enacted subsequent to the SC judgement, is before another bench headed by Justice Manoj Misra.

NEW DELHI: Former chief election commissioner (CEC) S Y Quraishi on Friday claimed that Form 6 cannot be filled by a deleted voter as it is meant only for new voters, though Election Commission officials contested this by citing Section 13(1) of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, which specifies Form 6 as the mode for filing claims for inclusion in the electoral roll.Posting the poll panel’s letter on the special drive for enrolment of “left out” electors in states/UTs where SIR is completed, on X, the former CEC said, “Form 6 can’t be filed by a deleted voter. The Supreme Court has already upheld the SIR process,” said an EC officer.
Article Summary: Former chief election commissioner S Y Quraishi on Friday claimed that Form 6 cannot be filled by a deleted voter as it is meant only for new voters. Article Title: EC orders special drive to add genuine electors 'left out' during SIR
Article Text:
An EC official said an average 10% of 800-900 electors per booth were deleted through SIR. Thus, each BLO will have to verify enrolment eligibility of less than 100 'deleted' voters.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Election Commission on Thursday ordered a special drive to identify and add back genuine electors who may have been "left out" during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) drive completed in 20 states, besides facilitating first-time or young electors.As part of the drive - meant to percolate to the grassroots the message that the deletions made during SIR, if erroneous, can be undone at any time by simply filling up Form 6 (for fresh enrolment) - booth level officers (BLOs) will visit homes of electors who were there in the pre-SIR electoral roll but were not included in the current electoral roll. They will, during these visits, ascertain the present status of such electors and facilitate their enrolment through Form 6, wherever a person is found to be eligible. This could be due to a valid eligibility proof not submitted earlier, corrected mapping to roll from last SIR, return of a shifted voter at registered address, or a young voter who has turned 18 since SIR, etc, said an official."Voter enrolment is a continuous process and any person not yet enrolled in the electoral roll or whose name has got deleted can apply for enrolment at any point of time. The objective of the special drive is to identify and facilitate such electors," EC said in a letter to state chief electoral officers (CEOs) Thursday.This followed a meeting held by EC with state/UT CEOs on Tuesday.As per the decision taken by the full commission on Sept 26, no declaration will need to be attached with Form 6 during the special drive.Nearly 7.7 crore voters were deleted across 13 states covered in SIR's first two phases, though net deletions came to around 5.6 crore. In Phase 3, completed in seven states, net deletions total nearly 24 lakh.The special drive's timing is significant as it comes days after a report in The Indian Express report alleged that election commissioners S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised questions over the SIR process in internal notes. However, the EC, in a statement released after a full commission meeting on Sept 26, placed it on record that all decisions related to SIR were unanimously approved by the CEC and the commissioners.The opposition, however, continues to amplify the issue, "unilaterally" blaming CEC Gyanesh Kumar for a "flawed" SIR, "unauthorised" changes to Form 6 and allegedly limited access of field officers to ECINet for making changes.Sources in the EC, however, told TOI Friday that the special drive is only in furtherance of the repeated directions by CEC to BLOs that "not a single Indian citizen who has completed 18 years of age should be left out of electoral roll".An EC official said an average 10% of 800-900 electors per booth were deleted through SIR. Thus, each BLO will have to verify enrolment eligibility of less than 100 "deleted" voters. With the EC instructing BLOs on Friday to visit the homes of 20-25 electors per week, house-to-house outreach and verification is expected to last a month.BLOs who visit the houses of deleted electors shall indicate the present status of each such elector in a list of absent, permanently shifted, deceased, duplicate and foreigner electors prepared by them. Electors for whom Form 6 has been filled up will also be indicated.They will share this list with booth level agents (BLAs) of recognised political parties and with electoral registration officers (EROs), along with the filled-up Form 6 and their field verification report. ERO is the competent authority to decide on addition or deletion.At the end of this exercise, the booth-wise lists prepared as above will also be shared by the EROs with the representatives of the political parties, giving them a further opportunity to enable enrolment of any left-out electors.Booth-level camps shall be organised to facilitate submission of applications for enrolment. Special camps may also be organised for enrolment of people living in night shelters, labour colonies and also for homeless & marginalised persons.As part of SIR completed in 20 states, a list of ASDD voters was prepared by each BLO with the probable reason for non-inclusion of their names. This list was displayed at the notice board of respective panchayat bhawans/urban local bodies and offices of the BDOs/panchayat, shared with the BLAs and with the political parties and also uploaded on the CEO website.Thereafter, the draft was published and shared with the political parties and uploaded on the CEO website. The final electoral roll was published after decisions on the claims and objections by the EROs and includes the list of electors that were added or deleted after the draft publication.
Article Summary: The Election Commission on Thursday ordered a special drive to identify and add back genuine electors who may have been "left out" during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) drive completed in 20 states. An EC official said an average 10% of 800-900 electors per booth were deleted through SIR. Thus, each BLO will have to verify enrolment eligibility of less than 100 'deleted' voters.
